content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon (especially 1–10 days ahead), especially when recent prices are falling.
- Overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 70→75+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to reflect mean reversion.
- Underestimates prices when recent 30-day average is low (e.g., <65), showing poor sensitivity to low-price regimes.
- Overestimates prices when recent 30-day average is high (e.g., >70), suggesting model lacks downward correction logic.
- Model exhibits lagged response to price drops — often underestimates a drop until 3–5 days after it occurs.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward lower prices in 30-day horizon, especially when historical volatility is high.
- Model fails to capture “mean reversion” in price clusters — tends to hold forecasts too high after a spike, then too low after a drop.
- When true price drops below 60, model often fails to adjust downward, especially if recent history was above 65.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike after minor price movements, then fails to correct.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon are often too optimistic when recent 30-day average is above 65, and too pessimistic when below 60.
